source_text: Fully connected layers use the same chain with $A=B=C=0$, $D=W$: $\begin{bmatrix}X_{k-1} & -W^{\top}\Lambda\\ -\Lambda W & 2\Lambda-X_k\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$. Pooling layers need their own incremental QCs. The paper takes the stride equal to the window length $\ell$, so the windows do not overlap. Averaging over one window is then $1/\sqrt\ell$-Lipschitz (Proposition 7: the averaging row $\tfrac1\ell\mathbf 1^{\top}$ has norm $\sqrt\ell/\ell$), and so is the whole layer, which acts on disjoint windows: square the per-window bounds and add. Being linear, average pooling admits full multiplier matrices; max pooling, $1$-Lipschitz under the same assumption (per window, $|\max_ia_i-\max_ib_i|\le\max_i|a_i-b_i|\le\|a-b\|$), admits only diagonal ones, the same distinction as in Section 5. Overlapping windows need a bound on the whole pooling operator: averaging the adjacent pairs of $(u_1,u_2,u_3)$ is the matrix $\tfrac12\begin{bmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{bmatrix}$, with norm $\sqrt3/2\gt1/\sqrt2$. For fully connected networks the layer-wise LMIs are equivalent to LipSDP (Remark 12, via chordal sparsity). For CNNs they are slightly more conservative than LipSDP on the unrolled network, but they hold for every input length and use multipliers of size $c$ instead of $cN$. In the experiments, LipSDP on the unrolled network was a little tighter for short signals, but its computation time grew quickly with the signal length, while the state-space SDP of a fully convolutional network does not grow at all. A fully connected head after flattening still sees all $c_pN_p$ features.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: The printed two-block fully connected LMI is the genuine A=B=C=0,D=W stateless specialization of the source dynamic layer certificate.
hypotheses: Arbitrary finite input/output dimensions; stateless state dimension0; diagonal activation multiplier.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: Actual matrix equality under a coordinate equivalence and a true PSD iff retain every block and both implication directions. A projection onto a subset of coordinates alone would not establish the source equivalence; the actual zero-state equivalence does.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: The fully connected certificate gives actual incremental weighted gain for the biased slope-restricted layer.
hypotheses: Arbitrary finite matrices/input pairs and bias; activation slope-restricted in[0,1]; nonnegative diagonal multiplier; actual certificate PosSemidef.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The literal quadratic form expands to weighted input minus output energy minus the real activation QC. Actual all-pair bias cancellation and scalar slope QC prove the weighted gain. This closes the FC layer specialization, without deriving the later general global-LipSDP chordal equivalence.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: For non-overlapping windows of positive length ell, actual averaging has gain1/sqrt(ell), and the actual averaging row has Euclidean normsqrt(ell)/ell.
hypotheses: Nonempty finite within-window coordinates and arbitrary finite disjoint window indices, represented by the product type; genuine L2/Euclidean norms.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The true coordinate average is analyzed by Cauchy-Schwarz. Squared per-window inequalities are summed over the actual disjoint-product coordinates and give the entire layer bound. The actual row norm equals both reciprocal-square-root and literal square-root-over-length expressions.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: For non-overlapping windows, the actual maximum satisfies|max a-max b|<=max_i|a_i-b_i|<=||a-b||2, and the whole disjoint layer is1-Lipschitz.
hypotheses: Nonempty finite windows, arbitrary finite disjoint window indices, genuine finite maximum and Euclidean norms.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: Actual maximizing coordinates yield the literal maximum-absolute-increment chain. Summing genuine squared window bounds establishes the all-pair whole-layer L2 bound; no overlapping coordinate reuse is included in that disjoint theorem.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Actual linear average pooling admits arbitrary PSD full channel multipliers; actual max pooling admits nonnegative diagonal multipliers, while allowing arbitrary PSD full multipliers is invalid in general.
hypotheses: Disjoint window channel maps; nonempty finite within-window coordinates; average multiplier is real PSD; max multiplier has nonnegative diagonal entries.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: An actual Gram factor and channel-matrix commutation prove the full average QC for arbitrary PSD channel weights. The genuine per-channel maximum QC sums with nonnegative diagonal weights. An actual PSD coupled multiplier and two true max-pooling inputs give QC=-1, disproving a universal full-PSD family. This does not claim that every conceivable valid multiplier for every special max map must be diagonal.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Averaging adjacent pairs of a real three-vector is exactly the displayed2x3 matrix with actual L2 operator normsqrt3/2>1/sqrt2.
hypotheses: Actual adjacent-pair average on arbitrary real three-coordinates; matrix spectral/L2 operator norm.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The output coordinates match the source operator exactly. A universal sum-of-squares gap proves the upper bound and the true input(1,2,1) attains it, yielding the genuine exact operator norm. Its strict comparison proves why the disjoint-window constant cannot be reused.
